en: From the *Zhongnan Mountain Assembly of Celestial Dragons*, the *Genealogy of the Monastic Community*, the *Origins of the Śākya Clan*, the *Genealogies of the Five Schools*, and the *Chart for Determining the Patriarchs* of the *Record of the Transmission of the Lamp*:
"The ancient Buddhas appeared in the world in an endless succession; it is impossible to know them all or to enumerate them exhaustively."
Therefore, while in recent times we speak of a thousand Tathāgatas within the Bhadrakalpa, from the time of Śākyamuni onwards, only seven Buddhas have been recorded.
According to the *Dīrgha Āgama*, it says: "The power of diligence of the seven Buddhas radiated light to extinguish the darkness;
each sat beneath a tree and therein attained perfect enlightenment. Furthermore, Mañjuśrī was the ancestral teacher of these seven Buddhas, the Great Being (Mahāsattva) Suṇhita of the Golden Flower.
While practicing the Way atop Mount Songshan, he was moved by a vision of the Seven Buddhas leading before him and Vimalakīrti following behind.

His present compositions begin with these Seven Buddhas; thus, tracing back to the *Bhadrakalpa*, from the time of the Seven Buddhas until the descent of Śākyamuni, he is regarded as the patriarch who transmitted the Dharma to India and China. He dwelt in this world for forty [years].
Nine years later, he addressed his disciple Mahākāśyapa:

"I have entrusted to you, in secret, the pure Dharma-eye, the wondrous mind of Nirvāṇa, the true reality beyond form—the subtle and sublime True Dharma—which does not rely on words and letters, but is transmitted separately outside the teachings."
"You must protect and uphold it. Furthermore, I charge Ānanda to act as my successor in transmitting the transformation, ensuring that it never be severed.
From this point on, there were twenty-eight successive generations until it was transmitted to Bodhidharma.

Later, Bodhidharma again carried the Single Branch of the True Dharma-Eye Treasury of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, along with the World-Honored One’s robe and bowl, crossing the sea from the west to arrive at Shaolin Temple on Mount Song in the east. He faced [the Emperor]...

Huike resided at the Wall Cave for nine years. He was also the founding patriarch of the Eastern Land. From him, the lineage descended in a continuous and flourishing succession, never ceasing from generation to generation.
The Second Patriarch was Chan Master Huike; the Third Patriarch was Chan Master Sengcan, the Mirror of Wisdom;
the Fourth Patriarch was Chan Master Daoxin, the Great Physician; the Fifth Patriarch was Chan Master Hongren, the Great Fulfillment; and the Sixth Patriarch was...
As for the Dharma Master Huineng, the Great Mirror: from the Sixth Patriarch downward, there emerged two lineages. One was the Dharma Master Qingyuan Xingsi;
the other was the Dharma Master Nanyue Huairang. It was these two masters who subsequently gave rise to the five schools.
He was the founding patriarch. From Qingyuan descended Chan Master Shitou Xiqian. Under Xiqian, two branches further emerged:
the first was Chan Master Yaoshan Weiyen, and the second was Chan Master Tianhuang Daowu.
Under Weiyen descended Chan Master Yunyan Tansheng. Under Tansheng descended Chan Master Dongshan Liangjie. Under Liangjie descended Cao Shan Benji.
From this, Master Jì established the Caodōn school. Under Tiānhuáng came Chóngxìn Chánshī of Lóngtán;
under Xìn came Xuānjiàn Chánshī of Dèshān; and under Jiàn came Yìcún Chánshī of Xuěfēng.
Below this, two further branches emerge: the first is Chan Master Xuansha Shibei; the second is Chan Master Yunmen Wenyan.
From these, the Yunmen school was subsequently established. Under Shibei emerged Chan Master Luohan Guichen;
under Guichen emerged Chan Master Qingliang Wenyi. After his passing, [a stupa] was erected for him, and he was posthumously titled Chan Master Dafa Yan.
The Master, from this point on, established the school of the Dharma Eye (Fayan). The three aforementioned schools all belong to the lineage of Qingyuan.
Furthermore, under Nanyue, there appeared the Chan Master Mazu Daoyi; from Daoyi emerged the Chan Master Baizhang Huaihai.
From below Hai, two branches further emerge. One is Chan Master Weishan Lingyou;
from You descend Chan Master Yangshan Huiji, by whom the Weiyang school was subsequently established. The other is Chan Master Huangbo Xiyun.
The lineage descends to Master Linji Yixuan, who thereby established the Linji school. These two aforementioned schools both belong to the lineage of Nanyue.
From the Sixth Patriarch downward, the lineages split into the two great branches of Qingyuan and Nanyue.
From these two great branches, they further divided into the five minor branches of Guiyang, Linji, Caodong, Yunmen, and Fayan.

These constitute the Five Schools, which correspond to the prophecy of "one flower and five petals. This is indeed the established pattern for the orderly succession of the celestial kinship, ensuring that the source is distant and the stream is long.
(Joyfully) Examining this according to the *Chuan deng lu*, it is the fifth generation after the Sixth Patriarch.

Furthermore, there were the Weiyang and Linji lineages; it was only in the sixth generation that the Caodong appeared, in the seventh generation that the Yunmen first emerged, and only in the ninth generation that the Fayan appeared.
Since later generations have become confused, how can they obscure the ancient sequence of their sources and lineages?

Therefore, I have carefully consulted the *Chuan deng lu* (Record of the Transmission of the Lamp) to compile this *Shishi yuanyou wuzong shipu dingzututu* (Genealogy of the Five Schools of the Śākya Lineage with Charts for Determining Patriarchs),

together with the dharma lineages of the five schools— both the direct branches and collateral offshoots— and how they followed the stream and divided into sects, tracing their origins back to the single skull-bowl from which they all descended.
These have been compiled into a single volume and entrusted to the press for publication throughout all quarters.

This shall enable future generations, from one generation to the next, to discern demonic delusions from the authentic, to abandon error and return to the correct, and to know that the transmission between teachers and disciples has its source, and the holding of the robe and bowl has its foundation.
This serves as the preface.
At this time,
on the Buddha’s Birthday during the first month of summer in the year of Kaimei (1703) of the Great Qing Kangxi era,
[the author] entered the Tiger Valley of Mount Zhongnan, twenty *li* southeast of the city of Huazhou in Xianyang Prefecture, Shaanxi, to ascend the summit.
About one *li* away is the ancient Panlongshan Temple. It is said that the monk Zichao Yuan, the thirty-third generation successor in the orthodox lineage of Linji, founded it.
Located fifteen *li* southwest of Huazhou City in Xianyang Prefecture, Shaanxi Province, one enters Zhongnan Mountain at Chidi Valley—also known as Majia Valley—which is now called [Xingfusi].
Imperially commissioned at Dayu, approximately twenty *li* from the Great Peak, at Tianlongshan Monastery. The Chan Master Xunlei Mingxi,
the thirty-fourth generation successor of the Linji orthodox lineage, together with monastics and laypeople from the ten directions,
bathed, burned incense, prostrated, compiled, and respectfully carved [this work].

The latter two schools are those that followed Nanyue. Tracing back from these through successive generations, we find that the fifth generation after the Sixth Patriarch includes both the Weiyang and Linji lineages;
the sixth generation is when the Caodong lineage first appears; the seventh generation is when the Yunmen lineage begins;
and the ninth generation is when the Fayan lineage finally emerges. What error could there be in this?

Wisdom, Rectitude, Universal Enlightenment, and Knowledge; Perfect Penetration, Tranquil Stillness, and Purity. He extensively expounds the nature of the Dharma-realm; his virtue is eternal.
Hongzong ○ To the thirteenth generation, Chan Master Fajian. His dharma-heir was Fucing, whose style name was Yunyan;
from him a collateral branch emerged (counting thirty characters).
The Master said: "His merit and great compassion are vast; he has universally perfected the path of the sages' awakening. His benefits are boundless, and his fundamental lineage flourishes forever.
His wondrous realization is eternally full; his self-nature realizes perfect fusion.

Furthermore, the fourteenth-generation master, World-Source Chan Master (Shijieyuan Chanshi), was the dharma heir of Menren Xingjin, whose style name was Bifeng. Additionally, a separate branch emerged from him (totaling forty-eight characters).
The lineage says: Wisdom is pure; virtue and morality are perfectly luminous. The ocean of the *tathatā*-nature is tranquil yet universally illuminating;

the source of the mind flows extensively and continuously; original enlightenment (*mūla-bodhi*) flourishes and prospers. The sacred fruit of the Benevolent One constantly unfolds in vast magnanimity; transmitting only the seal of the Dharma (*dharma-mudrā*), realization and awakening are harmoniously integrated.
Firmly upholding precepts and meditative concentration, one perpetually continues the ancestral tradition. Connecting to this lineage, another branch has newly continued (counting...):
(48 characters). The Master said:
"The Dharma-realm is profoundly still, vast, expansive, and majestic. It fills the fundamental awakening; one awakens to the essence of the mind.

Only when the spiritual is lucid and penetrating do essence and function flourish in abundance. Through hearing, contemplation, and cultivation, shamatha and vipashyana are ever in harmony. Transmitting and upholding these wondrous principles, one continues the legacy of the ancients."
The Honorable Xian: Faith, Understanding, Practice, and Realization; the moon brightens within the heavens.

Furthermore, under Mount Bifeng, the Second Generation Master of E’ou established the Wanshou Precept Platform at the Western Hills of Beijing, extending the single branch of Linji (this passage consists of twenty-four characters).
The Master said: "Pure and virtuous conduct; the accomplishment of the Buddha-dharma through letters; the wisdom of the Muni; the original self-nature; the perfectly luminous principle of practice;
the great penetration of the stage beyond learning. Furthermore, under the fourth-seventh generation patriarch of Bifeng was Master Ding Chan.
He entered Min and resided at Xuefeng Mountain. Furthermore, a branch lineage branched out from there (counting twenty characters).

The lineage says: "The Patriarch Cheng perfected precepts, concentration, and wisdom; he emitted light and realized perfect *pratyavekṣaṇā-jñāna*. His practice transcended the realization of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*); he thoroughly understood and awakened to true emptiness.
Also, under the thirteenth generation of Chan Master Zuding came Chan Master Mingcan, who entered Jin and resided there.
Zhongtiao Mountain, Wangu Temple. Furthermore, a branch extends transversely (counting twenty characters).
The lineage says: "Virtue is profound and mysterious; the nature-heaven is clearly revealed and vast. The lamp of wisdom links with the flames of the sea; Wangu shall be transmitted forever.
Furthermore, the thirteenth generation under Master Zu Ding Chan founded Jianzheng Temple in Shaanxi.
Fifteen li southwest of the city of Huazhou in Xian Prefecture, one enters Chidiyu (Valley of the Red Emperor) within Zhongnan Mountain.
It is also known as Majiayu (Valley of the Ma Family), and is now called Chideyu (Valley of Imperial Virtue). It is approximately twenty li from the Great Peak.

At Tianlongshan Monastery resides Chan Master Xunlei Mingxi, the thirty-fourth generation successor of the Linji orthodox lineage. In accordance with the established lineages of his predecessors, he... [descends].
Upon reaching the twentieth character, "Kong" (空), the sequence concludes with one additional branch (counting twenty characters in total). The subsequent branch states:

The seed of wisdom is the vajra fruit, Born upon the precious ground of devas and nāgas. The sprout of the mind excels under the rain of Dharma; When the flower blooms, the fruit is vast and numinous.

Under the Cao-Dong (Sōtō) school lies the ancestral temple of Shaolin. It comprises two lineages: that of Shaolin and that of Yuzhang in Jiangxi. Regarding the Yuzhang lineage (consisting of twenty-eight characters), its verse states:
"The ocean of pure awakening is perfectly vast and expansive; Awakening to the fundamental, eternal nature of wisdom is broad. The Way of the Patriarchs..."
The Dharma-eye flourished and was transmitted; it universally pervaded the sands of the world, bringing peace to the mind.

(Up to the twelfth generation, Master Huijing, who entered Shouchang in Jiangxi, from which a branch diverged—counting twenty-eight characters. The lineage says: Huizhao’s Way greatly promoted compassionate salvation;
Wuben transmitted the lamp, continuing the ancestral radiance. Xinghai’s profound clarity manifested the Dharma-realm; Guanghong propagated the practice far and wide.
May you realize the True and Constant. (From the *Jing* [Sutra], below, there also branches out the Great Master Yi of Boshan, who further continues one branch.

Perfectly capable of awakening, you belong to the vast, universal, and expansive lineage. Your Way rejoices in its identity with the Mysterious Ancestor. It is the ocean of pure *tathatā* (true suchness), profound stillness, and simple integrity.
Your virtuous conduct extends eternally; your wondrous essence is ever firm and solid. Your mind shines brightly upon the deep and obscure; your nature’s clarity reflects the sovereign mandate.

With a rectified heart, you bring auspicious blessings; through your reverence and sincerity, you vow to deliver others. With the snow-capped courtyard as your guide, you shall propagate [the Dharma] for them.
Taking Refuge on the Mysterious Path. (6th Generation; a branch extending from Pēng-qs Mountain at Hsing-hua Temple. Total: 20 characters. The lineage says:
"The ancestral Way is clarified through the cause of realization; the vast ocean of awakening is forever proclaimed. Universally delivering the great chiliocosm, all together ascend the Prajñā boat.
(1st Branch) Furthermore, below Ques Mountain, reaching the broad shore of the other side, a new branch emerged once more. (Total: 120 characters. The lineage:

It is said: The ocean of awakening is eternally vast; the transmission of the lineage is proclaimed and bestowed. The orthodox pulse extends afar; virtuous blessings flourish in abundance. Self-nature is all-pervasive; the original state is perfectly penetrating.

The wondrous principle of true wisdom is pure and limpid; the true mark is quiescent illumination. Through compassionate pity one benefits sentient beings, universally delivering them with impartiality.
Using the scales of the Vaipulya teachings, the instruction is initiated for the wise and sagely; through the practice of precepts, merit is achieved, and learning arises from awakening.

Attainment. The Dharma resides in the power of faith; through cessation and contemplation, concentration and wisdom, and the honoring of hearing, reflection, and cultivation, one adorns the stages and ranks.
Profoundly harmonizing with the ultimate truth, virtue is fulfilled and fruition is perfected. May the lamp of the Buddha’s teaching continue, upholding the Mind-Seal as a model for the world.

Such is my aspiration; may the world follow this example. Taking the Other Shore as its patriarch, these instructions are bequeathed to descendants, ensuring that posterity prospers as their predecessors did, enduring forever throughout ten thousand generations.

[This leads] to Chan Master Mingxin of Wujie, who further continued one branch (totaling sixteen characters). The lineage says: "His nature is vast and penetrating; his wondrous function is boundless.
He embodies the emptiness of ultimate reality, and the Way of the Patriarchs flourishes. Furthermore, there is Chan Master Wansong...
The Master later established one branch (counting twenty characters). The lineage says: Practice follows from wisdom and knowledge; penetrating through to enter the center of the ring;
transformation governs the three thousand worlds; widely opening the Dongshan school. Reaching Chan Master Zhìhóng, he further branched off another line (counting twenty characters).
The lineage says: Wisdom, faith, concentration, and virtue are treasures; resolve is good, realizing the practice of the Way; wondrous purity is the originally luminous truth; the True Dharma.

Vishisi Jing (also continuing the New Lineage): Reverently and diligently practice; when merit is perfected, blessings and joy follow. The lineage continues as a new lamp, realizing the self-nature of universal penetration.
Universally saving the great trichiliocosm, he holds the balance of the Caodong school. The robe and bowl have been transmitted; this is the ancestral command of Wansong.
Furthermore, Chan Master Miaoxiang Jueding branched off another line (counting twenty-eight characters). The lineage is called: Jingshan, Xiangran, Xi, and Jing.

The School: The myriad luminous precious jewels manifest as a brilliant lamp; the world’s bright moon proclaims its perfect illumination. Penetrating the heavens and realizing the Way, it spans heaven and earth.
This is the Yunmen lineage (counting twenty characters).

The Fayen lineage: Youtan followed Guangzheng; Liaoxing awakened to True Suchness (*tathatā*). Only when one’s virtues and wisdom are perfectly integrated does one truly know how to inherit the ancestral lamp.
(The Fayen lineage consists of twenty characters.)

The Pai school says: "The ancestral wisdom awakens to the fundamental truth; the Dharma-nature constantly gives rise to excellence. Samādhi and Prajñā are vast, perfect, and luminous; the ocean of awakening is a profound, pure seal.
These five schools and five lineages represent the original great outline of the tradition as it has circulated throughout the world. As for the others...

From the true branches and true leaves, lineages were grafted and schools divided; these relied solely upon the individual styles of various masters at a particular time, flourishing and prevailing according to circumstances as they established their own branches.
There are still more than thirty such houses, yet it is unknown from which original school they diverged, and up to this point, there has been no factual verification for them.
I have not arbitrarily included any of them. Those who come after must clarify what is correct.
Do not stray onto other paths. If you wish to exhaustively investigate the origins and the fundamental root, you should take this as your guide and standard.
Thus it is said. *The Genealogy of the World of the Black Robe:
A Gathering of the Heavenly Dragon Assembly on Mount Zhongnan* (End).
